messages:
maria: Heads-up — AcmeCorp (customer token ending ...9f) just reported repeated 429s from our /v1/rerank endpoint starting ~10:12 UTC. They say traffic was steady, no code changes on their side. Error snippet they sent: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\n{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}`. Can someone look?

alex: Do we have their request pattern? number of candidates per call and QPS? Also please paste request-id headers if available.

maria: Their example payload: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXXX9f' -d '{"query":"find best answers","candidates":["A","B","C",... 50 items]}'` — they said typical candidate list is 40-60 items, each request ~1 rps, but they have many tenants so bursts can land. They attached response headers: `x-ratelimit-limit: 2400`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-request-id: req_8f7a3c`.

jordan: Thanks — important detail: rerank internally scores each candidate which we bill/limit as N scoring ops. For large candidate lists the effective per-request quota burn is high. If their per-minute quota is 2400 scoring ops, 60 candidates = 60 ops per call so ~40 calls will exhaust it.

sam_oncall: I'm looking at ingress and rate-limiter logs for token XXXX9f. I see a burst between 10:11:30-10:13:00 where scoring ops/sec jumped x3 relative to baseline. Rate-limiter returned 429s starting at 10:12:05 with `policy=per_token_ops_per_minute`.

maria: Customer insists they didn't change anything. Could be a retry storm from their side or a background job kicked off. They say their app does occasional candidate-set refreshes.

alex: Quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily raise their quota for 1 hour to avoid customer impact, 2) apply an immediate soft-throttle on heavy requests (cap candidates per-call at 20) with an explanatory 429 body, or 3) suggest they change client to paginate candidates and/or dedupe. Which do we prefer?

jordan: I can push a short-lived quota increase via the admin console but need approval. Also we should confirm whether our rerank accounting changed in last deploy — checking deploy log.

support-bot: Deploy event: rerank-billing-adjust v2026.03.16 by eng-releases — changed internal scoring multiplier from 1.0 -> 1.0 (no-op). No recent deploys affecting counting.

sam_oncall: Metrics snapshot: node-pool-rerank-03 cpu spike aligns with burst. No OOMs. Rate-limiter shows many tokens hitting remaining=0 at same minute. Looks like legitimate consumption, not false positive.

maria: Customer also attached logs showing repeated 500->retry loops prior to the 429s. Could be their client retrying incorrectly.

alex: Action plan: 1) Ask customer for a sample request-id (we have req_8f7a3c already) and exact timestamps on their side. 2) Offer a one-hour quota bump while they root-cause. 3) Provide guidance to limit candidates per request and enable exponential backoff on 5xx/429.

jordan: I'll run a quick replay in staging with 60-candidate loads to confirm how many scoring ops are consumed and whether any accounting bug exists. Sharing repro curl below for internal testing:
```
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["c1","c2",...,"c60"]}' &
done
wait
```

sam_oncall: If you want me to escalate to infra, I can request temporary autoscale on dedicated rerank pool, but that might mask the root cause. We should prefer quota bump + customer-side changes first.

maria: I messaged the customer with the mitigation options and asked for their server-side logs and whether they started any batch jobs at ~10:10 UTC. They've replied they will check and asked for a temporary quota increase.

alex: Approved — grant +2x scoring ops quota for token ending ...9f for 1 hour. Please document escalation and TTL in the ticket. Also add a note to product: consider surfacing effective candidate-cost per-call in our API docs so customers understand burn rate.

jordan: Follow-up: I couldn't reproduce an accounting bug in staging — scoring ops scale linearly with candidate count as expected. Looks like the customer did a backfill job that triggered the burst.

maria: Customer confirmed they kicked off a backfill last night accidentally. They rolled it back. 429s stopped once we raised quota and they paused jobs. They asked for best practices. I sent guidance: cap candidates per-call, batch updates, add jittered exponential backoff and monitor `x-ratelimit-remaining`.

sam_oncall: Closing loop: I'll add a short KB note in support playbooks about rerank's candidate-cost behavior and an ops runbook for quick temporary quota adjustments. :white_check_mark: 

alex: Thanks team. Leaving this thread for doc updates and keep me posted if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
